title: Merge configuration layers and apply typed environment overrides
prompt: Implement deepMerge in src/merge.js, coerceEnvValue and applyEnv in src/env.js, and resolveConfig in src/config.js, then re-export deepMerge, coerceEnvValue, applyEnv, and resolveConfig from src/index.js. Use ES modules and only Node built-ins. A plain object is a non-null, non-array object whose prototype is Object.prototype or null. deepMerge(base, override) must return a new plain object with base and override recursively merged. Nested plain objects merge; arrays and all non-plain-object values replace earlier values; override properties whose value is undefined are skipped; null, false, 0, and the empty string are retained. Do not mutate either input, and deep-copy nested plain objects and arrays from the base so mutating the result cannot affect base. coerceEnvValue(value) requires a string and returns true for 'true', false for 'false', null for 'null', and a finite number for numeric strings matching an optional minus sign followed by either 0 or a non-zero digit plus more digits, optionally followed by a decimal point and one or more digits. Leading zeros such as '007', plus signs, exponents, whitespace, and a trailing dot are not numeric; all non-matching strings are returned unchanged. applyEnv(config, overrides) returns a new deep copy of config with dot-delimited string values from overrides applied at their nested paths. Paths must be non-empty and have no empty segments; override values must be strings. Apply keys in ascending code-unit order and throw an Error if a path traverses an existing non-plain-object value. resolveConfig(defaults, user = {}, env = {}) must merge defaults then user, then apply env, returning a new object without mutating any input.
